children: HOW MUCH BAD AI NEWS CAN WALL ST TAKE? BARCLAYS SAYS MORE THAN YOU THINK

AI optimism has helped propel US stocks to record highs, but investors increasingly worry that the market has become overly dependent on a handful of semiconductor companies to deliver the earnings growth needed to justify lofty valuations.

Those concerns have intensified as investors scrutinize the sustainability of data-center spending and look for evidence that billions of dollars being poured into AI infrastructure will generate adequate returns.

The broader debate is no longer whether AI will drive profits, but how vulnerable the US stock market is if the AI boom turns out to be less spectacular than investors expect. Barclays argues the answer may be: not very.

According to Barclays strategists led by Venu Krishna, semiconductor and hardware companies are expected to contribute more than half of the S&P 500's earnings growth over the next two years, highlighting the sector's outsized role in corporate America's profit engine.
Yet the brokerage's scenario analysis suggests the market has more of a cushion than investors might assume. Barclays estimates the S&P 500
could absorb a 15% downward revision to 2027 semiconductor earnings forecasts and still deliver above-trend profit growth.
Under that scenario, the index would still post roughly 12% earnings growth, challenging the notion that any disappointment in AI-linked sectors would necessarily derail the broader earnings outlook.
With most planned 2027 data-center capacity already under construction and AI demand still outstripping supply, Barclays sees limited risk to semiconductor earnings from potential project delays.
Main US indexes slide; Dow down most, off ~2%
All S&P 500 sectors red; healthcare weakest group
Dollar, bitcoin rise slightly; US crude up ~1%; gold down >1%
US 10-year Treasury yield edges down to ~5.06%
